name: Input tax credit — what it is and who may take it
definition: Input tax credit is the credit of input tax. Input tax is the central, State, integrated or Union territory tax charged on any supply of goods or services or both made to a registered person, and it includes IGST on imported goods and the tax payable by him under reverse charge, but excludes tax paid under the composition levy. A registered person is entitled to take that credit on supplies used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of his business, and the amount is credited to his electronic credit ledger.
why_it_exists: GST is a tax on value added. Without a credit for tax already borne on inputs, tax would compound at every stage of a supply chain. The credit is the mechanism that makes the levy fall on the margin rather than on the whole price at each stage.
inputs: tax charged on the inward supply, by head (CGST / SGST / IGST / UTGST)
whether the inward supply is used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of business
whether the tax was paid under the composition levy
outputs: an amount of input tax credit, by tax head
credit to the electronic credit ledger of the registered person
or a determination that no credit arises
preconditions: the claimant is a registered person under the CGST Act
the inward supply is a supply of goods or services or both made to him
common_mistakes: treating tax paid under the composition levy as input tax — s.2(62) expressly excludes it
taking credit of tax on a supply that is not used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of business
treating entitlement under s.16(1) as sufficient — s.16(2) is a separate, cumulative gate
booking the credit to the wrong tax head; the Act credits input tax by head, not as one pooled amount
legal_references: CGST Act 2017, s.2(63) — input tax credit
icai_references: NOT APPLICABLE — input tax credit is a statutory tax entitlement, not an accounting standard question
gst_references: CGST Act 2017, Chapter V (Input Tax Credit), ss.16 to 21
evidence_required: GSTIN of the recipient, showing he is registered
the inward supply document showing tax charged, by head
a business-use link for the inward supply
confidence_factors: weak when the document does not separate tax by head
weak when business use is asserted but not evidenced — s.155 places the burden of proof on the claimant
UNKNOWN — source is the Act as updated 31-08-2021; later amendments not held locally
validation_checks: the claimed credit does not exceed the tax charged on the document
the tax was not paid under the composition levy
each of the s.16(2) conditions is separately satisfied before the credit is taken
examples: a registered manufacturer buys raw material from a registered supplier who charges CGST and SGST; the material enters production — input tax within s.2(62), credit under s.16(1)
counterexamples: a registered person buys from a composition dealer — s.2(62) closes with 'but does not include the tax paid under the composition levy', so there is no input tax to credit

evidence.quote: in relation to a registered person, means the central tax, State tax, integrated tax or Union territory tax charged on any supply of goods or services or both made to him and includes
evidence.extraction_note: The defined term itself, rendered by the extractor as ―input tax‖ with substituted quotation glyphs, is quoted around rather than reproduced. The glyph artifact is in the extraction, not in the Act.

evidence.quote: the integrated goods and services tax charged on import of goods;
the tax payable under the provisions of sub-sections (3) and (4) of section 9;
but does not include the tax paid under the composition levy;
means the credit of input tax;
means any goods other than capital goods used or intended to be used by a supplier in the course or furtherance of business;
means any service used or intended to be used by a supplier in the course or furtherance of business;
means goods, the value of which is capitalised in the books of account of the person claiming the input tax credit and which are used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of business;

Every registered person shall, subject to such conditions and restrictions as may be prescribed and in the manner specified in section 49, be entitled to take credit of input tax charged on any supply of goods or services or both to him which are used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of his business and the said amount shall be credited to the electronic credit ledger of such person.
Where any person claims that he is eligible for input tax credit under this Act, the burden of proving such claim shall lie on such person.
